newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's outlines U.S. dollar solvency test.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's outlines U.S. dollar solvency test.

text.p: Lloyd's of London on Tuesday said that members would have to undergo a U.S. dollar solvency test to establish whether their dollar profits for 1994 could be released from the Lloyd's American Trust Funds (LATFs).

Members will be subject to the solvency test in April 1997 based on the declared results of syndicates for the 1994 year of account, including run-off results arising from 1993 and 1994 syndicates and open-year balances from 1995 syndicates.
Only where this test shows an overall surplus will members' U.S. dollar profits in respect of the 1994 year, including previous releases, be released.
LATF holds premiums and other payments made by underwriting names for insurance policies payable in dollars.

Because of the complex requirements on U.S. dollar solvency test filing and the fact that certain syndicate non-cash assets may not be admitted, it could reduce the released dollar profits and could affect the performance of quoted Lloyds corporate members.
As a result of the treatment of certain non-cash assets as non-admitted assets, not all of members' dollar profits may be released for distribution.
Any dollars retained in members' LATFs would have to be held until the completion of the next LATF U.S. dollar solvency test in 1998.
Under the the U.S. regulatory system Lloyd's syndicates has to lodge dollar funds gross of reinsurance recoveries. Until a claim is actually made, any potential recovery is disallowed.
